origins: Testimonies that jump from “then” to “now,” cheerful greetings, and unspoken rules about “fine” teach us that struggle is a mark against faith. People hide anxiety, doubt, marriage trouble, and sin, so everyone appears to be doing well alone.
teaches: Scripture is full of struggling believers. Paul writes, “For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,” and “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” He adds, “when I am weak, then I am strong.” Elijah prayed that he might die, and God sent an angel to say, “Get up and eat.” The psalmist says, “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted.” Struggle is not the opposite of faith. It is often where faith is exercised and grace is found.
self_statements: Everyone else at church has it together.
If I struggle, my faith is weak.
I must say I am fine.
Real Christians do not feel this way.
I would be judged if they knew.
errors: Believing I am either strong in faith or failing.
Assuming others would judge my struggles.
Feeling ashamed and concluding that I am a bad Christian.
Predicting that I would be rejected if I were honest.
questions: Where did I learn that Christians should not struggle?
Which people in Scripture struggled, and how did God treat them?
What do I think when I see someone else struggling?
What does it cost me to say “fine” every week?
Who might be safe to be honest with?
What does God say to the weary?
truth: Struggle does not disqualify me. God’s grace meets me in weakness, and I can be honest with safe people. Honesty makes the church stronger.
hw_truths: God’s grace is sufficient for me.
Weakness is where Christ’s power rests.
The Lord is near to the brokenhearted.
I can be honest with a safe person.
log: Each week, note one time you were honest about a struggle.
actions: Write five and what God did.
Say it when you feel you must hide.
prayer: Lord, I have hidden my struggles to look strong. Thank You for meeting me in weakness. Give me courage to be honest with safe people. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I think of others who struggle?
What does God say to the weary?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God’s grace is sufficient for me in my weakness.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Good Christians never struggle.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
